subject: Transformation of oridnal ipsative data for two-factor CFA model in Lavaan

messages.author: 6bbbdc207a0d3bf6
messages.subject: Transformation of oridnal ipsative data for two-factor CFA model in Lavaan
parts:
Hello,

I'm new to the world of structural equation modelling, and I'm currently working with a questionnaire dataset aimed at understanding the factors influencing pro-environmental behaviours. To analyse this dataset, I'm utilising the Schwartz Value Scale statements.

The questionnaire comprises eight statements, with four statements, each contributing to self-transcendence and self-enhancement values. 

My intention is to employ a two-factor CFA model. However, there's a challenge I'm facing with my questionnaire – it's based on a forced-choice format. Respondents were asked to rank these statements from 1 (least preferred) to 8 (most preferred). Consequently, my data has taken on an ordinal ipsative nature, where the sums and means remain constant.

 I came across a couple of papers that suggest methods for transforming ordinal ipsative data to make it suitable for factor analysis. For instance, Chan and Bentler (1998) proposed a method for this transformation in their paper titled "Covariance Structure Analysis of Ordinal Ipsative Data."

Chan, W., Bentler, P.M. Covariance structure analysis of ordinal ipsative data. Psychometrika 63, 369–399 (1998). https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02294861

Is it possible to conduct this transformation in Lavaan? I apologise if this seems like a basic question, as I'm quite new to this type of analysis and still in the learning process.

Best regards,

Bhavendu
